title: Nearly all surveyed pathway models have memory; very small networks may not

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Nearly all surveyed pathway models have memory; very small networks may not

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Memory was found in all but four of the 35 surveyed BioModels pathway models, and three of those four had fewer than four nodes, suggesting that very small networks either cannot have, or are very unlikely to have, memory.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Overall, we found memory models in all surveyed biological networks except four models, of which three had a low number of nodes (<4) suggesting that too small networks either cannot, or are very unlikely to, have memory

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.1. Biological Networks May Possess Multiple Types of Memory”. Scope: 35 ODE pathway models from BioModels

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The exact survey count is directly reproducible. The broader suggestion that very small networks cannot or rarely can have memory is weakly identified by this small, selected sample.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rerun all memory tests on the 35 models and relate absence of memory to node count. The reported counts are confirmed by replication, while the general small-network inference requires a larger, systematically sampled model set.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Only four negative cases support the network-size suggestion.

Model selection and minimum three-node testing requirements confound size.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.94
discriminating power: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.82
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The exception count among the 35 models is a direct rerun. The further claim that very small networks cannot or almost never have memory is an extrapolation from three cases and is not covered by a size-balanced public sample. Only the census half is well powered.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rerun the memory screen and count how many of the 35 models lack every memory type, then record the node counts of those exceptions and of a broader set of BioModels with fewer than four nodes. All-but-four, with three of the four below four nodes, would confirm the census; memory in most sub-four-node models, or a different exception count, would refute the size suggestion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Three small exceptions do not separate 'cannot have memory' from 'this assay missed it'.

The surveyed set was not built as a systematic sweep of network size.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.55
data existence: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.8
